Ana: Heads up — putting up a lightweight proposal for catalog lifecycle updates: 'soft pin' tier, 30d benchmark window, customer migration SLAs. Need product + eng + SE sign-off before Q2 roadmap finalization. Sketch below.

Ana:
``` 
Proposal:
- onboarding: 2-phase: smoke bench (10 samples) -> full cohort (100 samples)
- soft-pin: 14d soft pin with auto-notify + migration credits
- deprecations: 90d public notice + canary for top 10 tenants
- acceptance: quality delta <= 2% across eval set OR manual review
- metrics: perf (p50/p95), regression on core prompts, cost delta
```

Mike: Quick Q — who owns canary ops? Eng-runtime or SRE? I'd suggest eng-runtime builds the job but SRE runs it until we automate.

Sophia: From customer/SE side we need an opt-in migration window + a way for customers to request a 'hold' if they have contractual reasons. Also recommend offering a 2-week migration credit for enterprise customers.

Kevin: Risk callout: regional L10n models have hardware/quantization skew. Suggest: soft-pin only for global models; regionals require explicit hard-pin or partner coordination.

Ana: Agreed. Action items:
1) Eng -> draft canary job and rollback playbook (owner: Mike).
2) Product -> draft comms + migration credit framework (owner: Sophia).
3) Legal/Commercial -> confirm contract 'hold' flow (owner: Kevin).
Deadline: Tue next week EOD.

Mike:
```bash
# local canary run snippet
./canary-run --cohort=top10 --duration=48h --metrics=latency,p95,quality_delta
```

Sophia: :thumbsup: SE will prep FAQ + migration flow docs.

deploy-bot: INF-3482 created: canary-runbook (assignee: Mike)

Ana: If no objections by EOD Friday we'll fold this into the roadmap. @Kevin tagging for commercial constraints.

Kevin: No objections from my side; will escalate if any contract conflicts surface.
